Traced Score

How we calculate your Traced Score

001

Your Traced Score summarizes your overall exposure profile in a single number, from 0 to 10. It compares your levels of essential elements against your levels of toxic elements, measured relative to a global reference database. Here is how we get there.

002

First, we compare each element measured in your hair against that reference database. This shows where your levels sit relative to a broader population, element by element.

003

Next, we look for patterns. Elements rarely move on their own, so we use statistical modeling to find the ones that tend to rise and fall together. From those patterns, we draw out two underlying measures: one that summarizes your essential elements and one that summarizes your toxic elements.

004

Your Traced Score brings these two measures together, weighing your essential elements against your toxic ones. A higher score indicates fewer exposure elements flagged for review. A lower score indicates greater potential to review everyday exposure sources and essential element levels.

005

Because hair can reflect both what moves through your body and what it comes into contact with, your score is best read as a starting point, not a conclusion. It is not a measure of your health or a diagnosis of any condition. It is meant to inform, not advise.

Terms and Conditions Privacy Policy

Traced is an exposure assessment laboratory test that measures selected elements in a hair sample and provides an informational report comparing the measured results to a reference database. It is intended to help individuals understand elemental patterns measured in their hair and learn about common environmental, dietary, and lifestyle sources associated with those elements. Results are presented for educational and informational purposes only. The test is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease or medical condition and the test results should not be used as a substitute for professional medical advice. The test has not been evaluated or approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA).
